note: Thinking Inertia (arXiv 2610.11765v1, 8 Oct 2026, preprint, not peer reviewed). Data numbers on screen: 99.7% (explicit inference rate on open-ended math with thinking mode off and no extra prompt, M2), 62% (same tasks and judge with thinking mode off plus the strict prompt, M5) and about 15 points (drop in mean open-ended accuracy from M2 to M5 across the five models with fully disabled thinking). All are the authors' runs at temperature 0. Explicit inference is labelled by a blinded GPT-5.5 judge and cross-checked with Claude Opus 4.8 and five human annotators (sec 3.6, App. D). Every rate is about visible output only; the video makes no claim about computation inside the model or about compute savings (sec 5.1, sec 5.2). Every other digit on screen is part of a model or benchmark name (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-235B, GSM8K), a source tag (section, page, table, figure), the arXiv id or its version.

numbers.99.7: Explicit Inference Rate on open-ended tasks (GSM8K and MATH) under M2 THINK-OFF (thinking mode disabled, no prompt change), pooled over all outputs of all six models: 99.69% with the GPT-5.5 judge (Table D.3, p. 23; sec 3.3, p. 11). Rounded to 99.7. Per model it is 99.5 to 99.9% (Figure H.1, p. 32; Table H.2, p. 33), so it holds for each model, not only pooled; the l05 tag 'each model: about the same' rests on that range. Gemini-3-Flash runs at 'minimal', not off, in Modes 2 to 6 (Table B.2, p. 21): the 'Gemini-3-Flash: minimal' tag. Shown in l05 and again, small, as the 'before' value in l08 with the tag 'no extra prompt'.
numbers.62: Explicit Inference Rate on open-ended tasks under M5 STRICT (thinking mode disabled plus 'Give the final answer directly without any reasoning.'), pooled over all outputs: 62.00% with the GPT-5.5 judge (Table D.3, p. 23; sec 3.3, p. 11). Claude Opus 4.8 gives 61.02%. Pooled: the local Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-32B runs use full splits and so carry about 60% of the open-ended outputs (Table B.1, p. 21). Per model it varies a lot: Qwen3-4B 97.78%, Qwen3-32B 56.73%, Qwen3-235B 98.90% (Table H.2, p. 33); GPT-5.4 is almost fully answer-only under M5 (ETR 100 and 99.8 on GSM8K and MATH, Figure G.2, p. 31). Hence the tags 'pooled over all replies' and 'varies by model', and the line says 'most replies', never 'most models'. Includes Gemini-3-Flash at minimal: tag 'Gemini-3-Flash: minimal'.
numbers.15: (1) 'mean accuracy by about 15 percentage points': moving from M2 to M5 on open-ended tasks 'across the five LLMs with fully disabled thinking' (sec 1, p. 3; sec 3.3, p. 11: 'Across models with a disabled-thinking condition ... reduces mean accuracy by about 15 percentage points on Open-ended tasks'). A five-model mean, Gemini-3-Flash excluded (tag 'Gemini-3-Flash not in the mean'). Per model (Figure G.2, p. 31): GSM8K +0.1, -49.0, +0.9, -25.1, -22.7; MATH +0.5, -6.2, -1.8, -16.9, -28.5 (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GPT-5.4): tag 'varies by model'. Shown as 'about -15 points' with 'mean of five models'. (2) page 15, the l14 receipt label 'sec 5.1, p. 15'.

drawing_only._bool / _mcq: 5.15 and 45.57: pooled M2 explicit inference rates on yes-or-no and multiple choice (Table D.3, p. 23; sec 3.3, p. 11), spoken as 'rarely' and 'almost half'. claims.l01: A question, so it asserts nothing. It is the paper's title as a question ('LLMs Keep Thinking When Told Not To'). The chat bubble shows the p. 13 question wording without digits ('find the area of the rectangle') and the M5 prompt from Table 2 (p. 7); the reply that fills with lines is the open-ended column of the p. 13 example under M5 (Qwen3-32B writes the full solution). No number is attached to the hook.
claims.l02: Table 3 (p. 8) and Table B.2 (p. 21): six models; Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-235B-A22B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GPT-5.4 have thinking disabled or 'none' in Modes 2 to 6; Gemini-3-Flash(-Preview) uses 'minimal', 'treated as near-off rather than strict off'. Six benchmarks in three answer spaces (sec 3.1, p. 8): BoolQ, StrategyQA (yes-or-no), MMLU, MMLU-Pro (multiple choice), GSM8K, MATH (open-ended; both are math, hence 'open-ended (math)').
claims.l03: Sec 2.3 (pp. 5 to 6) and Table 1: a blinded LLM judge (GPT-5.5, sec 3.1) labels the visible pre-answer text; only 'Explicit reasoning' (deduction, computation, comparison, elimination, rule application, evidence-to-conclusion, causality addressing Q) counts toward EIR. A generic lead-in such as 'The answer is' is not counted (sec 2.3, p. 5; Figure 3 case 3). 'A step from question to answer' is the plain form of 'an explicit inferential step that addresses Q' (sec 1, p. 3).
claims.l04: Table D.3 (p. 23), M2, pooled over all outputs: yes-or-no 5.15% ('rarely'), multiple choice 45.57% ('almost half'). The line says 'Across all replies' because the six-model means differ (multiple choice about 55%: Figure H.1 and Table H.2). Per model, multiple choice ranges from 5.3% (GPT-5.4) to 88.9% (Gemini) (Figure H.1, p. 32).
claims.l05: Table D.3 (p. 23), M2 open-ended 99.69%, pooled; 99.5 to 99.9% per model (Figure H.1, Table H.2). 'With no extra prompt' names the M2 condition (Table 2: 'None.'), so it stays apart from the strict prompt in l07 and l08. Open-ended means GSM8K and MATH.
claims.l06: Sec 3.2 (p. 9), receipt crop, the authors' italic summary: 'We use “thinking inertia” to describe how visible explicit inference persists under no-thinking controls and becomes more common as the answer space opens.' The crop holds only that PDF line, no digits.
claims.l07: Table 2 (p. 7), M5 STRICT: 'Give the final answer directly without any reasoning.' with enable_thinking off. The thinking mode toggle stays OFF on screen.
claims.l08: Table D.3 (p. 23): M5 open-ended 62.00% (GPT-5.5 judge), pooled; 'still most replies' because 62% is over half of all open-ended replies. Tags 'pooled over all replies' and 'varies by model' (Table H.2: 56.73% to 98.90% for the Qwen models; GPT-5.4 almost fully answer-only per Figure G.2). The human annotators' rate on the sampled M5 open-ended cell is 57.1% (Table 5, p. 14), also over half.
claims.l09: Sec 1 (p. 3) and sec 3.3 (p. 11): across the five models with fully disabled thinking, M2 to M5 'reduces mean accuracy by about 15 percentage points' on open-ended tasks. The seesaw base reads 'open-ended math'; sec 3.3 reports little accuracy change on yes-or-no and multiple choice. The per-model changes vary from about zero to -49.0 (Figure G.2): tag 'varies by model'. The seesaw tilt is schematic and carries no value; no red or green.
claims.l10: Sec 3.3 (p. 11), receipt crop, bold run-in: 'On open-ended tasks, no-thinking comes at a cost.' The crop holds only that PDF line ('... This pattern is consistent with greater computational'); the paragraph above with the pooled rates is outside it. The 'cost' price tag repeats the paper's word.
claims.l11: The full-page figure on p. 13: one MMLU geometry item rewritten as Boolean verification, multiple choice and open-ended, Qwen3-32B in six modes. The video shows the M5 (strict prompt) row. Tag 'one example: Qwen3-32B, p. 13'. The rectangle is drawn without numbers.
claims.l12: P. 13, M5 row: the Boolean form returns only \boxed{yes} and the multiple-choice form only \boxed{C}, both with a green check for strict answer-only; the open-ended form writes the full Pythagorean solution before \boxed{50}. One item, one model. The hand taps 'yes' and 'C', the answers in the figure.
claims.l13: Sec 3.5 (p. 12), receipt crop, the authors' italic summary: 'Even for the same question, the answer space shapes whether an LLM answers directly.' The highlight stops before 'an LLM'; the narration says 'a model'. The claim rests on Figure 6 (Qwen3-32B, M2 thinking mode off, matched numeric MMLU/MMLU-Pro items), not on the p. 13 strict-prompt example; the scope tag 'Fig 6: Qwen3-32B, thinking mode off, matched math items' is on screen while the receipt is up.
claims.l14: Sec 5.1 (p. 15), receipt crop: 'Our claims therefore concern visible output, not the absence of task-relevant computation from hidden states.' The highlight covers 'Our claims therefore concern visible output'. The closed box and the '?' show that the paper does not look inside; no claim either way.
claims.l15: Advice framed as a condition, not a recommendation to use answer-only prompts: sec 5.2 (p. 16) suggests answering directly only 'when the interface provides sufficient support' and warns that visible compliance does not mean lower inference cost. 'Read what comes before it' points at the pre-answer text the paper measures. End credit: arXiv id, v1, unofficial explainer.
